title: Kamarupa and Davaka appear separately
evidence: Allahabad prasasti names both among frontier rulers paying tribute and showing obedience.
interpretation: Separate polities; no territorial outline and no named Kamarupa king.

title: Beginning of the historical Varman genealogy
evidence: Seventh-century genealogies name Pushyavarman as the historical ancestor.
interpretation: Working origin around Guwahati / lower Brahmaputra valley; founding year and complete original territory unknown.
limitation: Do not state that the Allahabad inscription names Pushyavarman.

title: Incorporation of the Kopili–Jamuna country
evidence: Davaka is separate in the fourth-century record; later Kamarupa evidence occurs in this area.
interpretation: Kalyanavarman, Mahendravarman and Bhutivarman are differently emphasised in reconstructions.
map_representation: dated evidence points; gradual uncertain expansion
limitation: Do not animate 428 or 470 as a securely dated annexation.

title: Reported embassy from a Kapili country
evidence: Bhattasali discusses the Chinese notice and uncertain identification.
interpretation: Attribution specifically to Kalyanavarman is a historical identification, not a recorded conquest.
limitation: Diplomacy cannot date absorption of Davaka.

title: Bhutivarman’s Barganga authority
evidence: Corrected text records an asrama founded by a district officer for the king’s longevity.
interpretation: Supports local royal administration and an asvamedha claim; not conquest of a named Bengal province.
map_representation: inscription locality; no Bengal conquest polygon
limitation: The earlier 553–554 CE reading was rejected; no Gupta-era date remains in the revised text.

title: Original Mayurasalmala grant
evidence: Nidhanpur charter recalls Bhutivarman’s earlier gift in Chandrapuri district.
interpretation: Land-grant authority; Sylhet identification widely used, with older alternative localisations.
limitation: Does not establish conquest of all Sylhet, Ratnapitha or Pundravardhana.

title: Proposed western expansion into Pundravardhana
evidence: Older histories interpret grant geography and Gupta decline as expansion.
interpretation: Possible historical reconstruction; no explicit conquest statement or date in Barganga.
limitation: Do not use c.550 as a verified acquisition year.

title: Mahasenagupta’s victory over Susthitavarman
evidence: Aphsad inscription’s retrospective victory is discussed in the Dubi edition.
interpretation: A defeat is supported; extent of occupation or western territorial loss is not enumerated.
limitation: Loss of all Pundravardhana is an additional inference.

date_label: Before Bhaskara’s mature rule; c.600 context
title: Gauda invasion and capture of the brothers
evidence: Dubi charter narrates defeat, captivity and return.
interpretation: Temporary subordination is the editor’s interpretation; the invading king’s identification needs caution.
limitation: Do not merge automatically with Mahasenagupta’s separate victory notice.

date_label: Early Bhaskara reign; exact year unknown
title: Recovery of political independence from Gauda
evidence: Dubi praise and later political conduct support reassertion after captivity.
interpretation: Recovery of Kamarupa independence; not an explicitly dated reconquest of a named Bengal province.
map_representation: independence status change with uncertain date
limitation: Keep independence and territorial acquisition as separate concepts.

title: Alliance with Harshavardhana
evidence: Harshacharita’s embassy and alliance are discussed in the inscription edition.
interpretation: Diplomatic alignment explains later Gauda campaigns.
limitation: An alliance is not a transfer of Harsha’s territory.

date_label: Later Bhaskara reign; often placed c.638–643, disputed
title: Victory camp at Karnasuvarna
evidence: Nidhanpur opening names the royal victory camp at Karnasuvarna.
interpretation: Strong evidence of presence / temporary possession; full area and duration unknown.
map_representation: camp point; optional uncertain campaign reach
source_locator: Opening formula; compare Sircar EI XXX p.296
limitation: Nidhanpur has no secure CE issue date. Do not label 643 as after Harsha’s death in 647.

title: Renewal of Bhutivarman’s land grant
evidence: The charter reinstates tax-free grant rights after the earlier plates were lost/destroyed.
interpretation: Administrative act involving Chandrapuri; not proof that it had just been militarily reconquered.
map_representation: grant symbol linked to camp and findspot
limitation: Document replacement is not a reconquest event.

title: Traveller distinguishes Pundravardhana and Kamarupa
evidence: Travels east from Pundravardhana across a large river; describes Kamarupa separately.
interpretation: Important western geographic anchor; 10000-li circuit is not a survey.
limitation: Separate country descriptions are not themselves a record of Kamarupa losing a province.

title: Nalanda seal attests long-distance connection
evidence: Seal with the royal genealogy is known from Nalanda finds.
interpretation: Royal communication or religious/diplomatic contact; territorial conquest is not established.
limitation: Do not add Magadha or Nalanda to controlled territory on this basis.

title: Salastambha line replaces the Varmans
evidence: Later dynastic records recall Salastambha’s accession.
interpretation: Dynastic change; does not date loss of Gauda or all outlying territories.
limitation: Foundation of Hadapesvara as capital is not securely dated to accession day.

title: End of Bhaskara’s Gauda possession is not securely dated
evidence: Other seventh-century rulers also use Karnasuvarna.
interpretation: Evidence does not establish a single documented handover or a 650 reconquest by a named opponent.
map_representation: end-date unknown; do not carry occupation to 725
limitation: Broad bounds are a research window, not a proposed period of continuous occupation.

title: Lordship over Gauda, Odra, Kalinga and Kosala
evidence: Pasupati record names Harshadeva of the Bhagadatta line in the royal marriage genealogy.
interpretation: Significant external-reach claim; duration and administrative occupation unknown.
map_representation: separate named claim regions; no continuous empire fill
limitation: Do not turn the four place-names into a surveyed corridor or a Ratnapitha reconquest date.

title: Nepal–Kamarupa marriage connection
evidence: Rajyamati is identified as Harshadeva’s daughter and Jayadeva’s queen.
interpretation: Dynastic marriage; Nepal is not thereby annexed.
limitation: Older 759-era conversion should not be silently mixed with modern 733 usage.

date_label: During Bengal king Devapala’s reign; exact date unknown
title: Bengal Pala claim of Pragjyotisha submission
evidence: Bhagalpur plate says the Pragjyotisha ruler accepted Jayapala’s command without battle.
interpretation: Political submission claim; direct annexation and province-sized losses are not stated.
map_representation: suzerainty marker; no hard annexation polygon
limitation: The Bengal general Jayapala is not the later Kamarupa king Jayapala.

title: Tezpur rock inscription
evidence: Dated record of royal regulation associated with river traffic.
interpretation: Secure chronological anchor and local authority; not the realm’s eastern frontier.
limitation: Regulation of a locality does not delimit the whole kingdom.

title: Parbatiya charter: north-bank grant
evidence: Grant issued at Hadapesvara; Haposa in Svalpa-Mangoka of Uttara-kula.
interpretation: North-bank administration; exact Haposa location remains uncertain.
map_representation: approximate grant district and capital region
limitation: The charter is not absolutely dated.

title: Proposed renewed North Bengal authority
evidence: Older histories identify grant places / river names with North Bengal.
interpretation: A proposed reassertion, not an explicit record that Pundravardhana was reconquered.
limitation: Keep different Vanamala grants separate; Parbatiya is not proof of all other identifications.

title: Foundation of Kamarupa Pala line
evidence: Later charters recall selection of Brahmapala after Tyagasimha’s heirless death.
interpretation: Founder of the Pala line, not the Varman line; the administrative-service story is unverified.
limitation: Wide numeric bounds record chronology disagreement, not a 120-year reign.

title: From Hadapesvara to Sri Durjaya
evidence: Early Saratbari charter uses Hadapesvara; later Bargaon/Sualkuchi records use Durjaya.
interpretation: Supports a capital change; cannot establish that Tezpur was simply renamed Durjaya.
limitation: Durjaya is commonly placed near Guwahati; exact archaeological site requires confirmation.

title: Ratnapala’s victory over Rajyapala
evidence: Gachtal genealogy reports the victory and Ganges advance.
interpretation: Major westward military episode; no precise annexed province or occupation interval is supplied.
limitation: Not proof of permanent annexation of Bengal or recovery of all Ratnapitha.

title: Chandra campaign reaches Kamarupa / Lauhitya
evidence: Paschimbhag and related Chandra praise describe the expedition.
interpretation: An opposing campaign missing from a one-sided expansion narrative; duration and occupiable area unknown.
limitation: Synchronising the opposing king specifically with Ratnapala depends on chronology.

title: Chandra administration in Srihatta
evidence: Paschimbhag grant places Srihatta-mandala and its districts within Pundravardhana-bhukti.
interpretation: Direct administrative counter-evidence to uninterrupted Kamarupa rule in Sylhet.
limitation: Does not date exactly when Bhutivarman’s former grant region changed hands.

title: Indrapala defeats Kalyanachandra
evidence: Gachtal genealogy reports a victory involving a fleet.
interpretation: Military success; battlefield and annexed land remain unlocated.
map_representation: naval victory event; no guessed route
limitation: Indrapala’s textbook reign c.960–990 is approximate; do not force the battle into 975.

title: Guwakuchi grant and beneficiary provenance
evidence: Charter concerns Pandaribhumi in Mandi-visaya of Uttara-kula; donee’s origin is discussed separately.
interpretation: A Brahmana from Sravasti does not make the donated village part of Sravasti or Pundravardhana.
limitation: Full fresh collation of Guwakuchi was not completed; broad Bengal inference is not accepted as proved.

date_label: Vigrahapala III, regnal year 11; CE conversion variable
title: Bengal Pala administration in Pundravardhana
evidence: Belwa charter explicitly names Pundravardhana-bhukti and subordinate units.
interpretation: Secure administrative foothold of the Bengal Palas; not proof of who controlled every part of the wider province.
limitation: Regnal date must not be promoted to an exact territorial transfer year.

title: Jatavarman’s success against Kamarupa
evidence: Belava verse 8 praises success against Kamarupa; reference article leaves the opponent unidentified.
interpretation: Some histories infer seizure of part of Pundravardhana; exact parcel, ruler and date unresolved.
map_representation: conflict event; optional uncertain loss annotation
limitation: Harshapala c.1015–1035 cannot be paired uncritically with Jatavarman c.1050–1075.

date_label: Dharmapala episode; proposed only; chronology disputed
title: Claim that Dharmapala recovered the lost territory
evidence: A circulated teaching narrative says Dharmapala soon recovered it.
interpretation: Keep as an unresolved claim until a specific charter passage and defensible locality identification support it.
map_representation: research note only; no ownership change
limitation: No confirmed reconquest year, parcel or primary conquest statement was established in this review.

title: Dharmapala’s grant geography and Kamarupanagara
evidence: Khonamukh, Subhankarapataka and Pushpabhadra records are associated with his reign.
interpretation: Grant locality identifications must precede a claim of North Bengal recovery; Dijjina/Diju identification is contested.
limitation: Full fresh collation of the three charters remains a priority; they are not automatically reconquest deeds.

date_label: Late 11th / early 12th century; exact campaign year unknown
title: Ramapala’s advance against Kamarupa
evidence: Ramacharita tradition and later history record conquest of Kamarupa or part of it.
interpretation: Extent disputed; restriction solely to North Bengal is one reconstruction, not a settled boundary.
limitation: The project’s 1110 line and Manas border are editorial choices, not recorded survey limits.

date_label: Under Ramapala/Kumarapala; sequence clearer than year
title: Tingyadeva’s rule and subsequent revolt
evidence: Kamauli narrative explains Vaidyadeva’s appointment after disloyalty in the eastern possessions.
interpretation: Evidence for the Pala intervention sequence; administrative seat and full governed area need localisation.
limitation: Do not equate the entire eastern possessions with one fixed Ratnapitha polygon.

date_label: Vaidyadeva; Kamauli regnal year 4; absolute conversion debated
title: Vaidyadeva replaces the rebellious ruler
evidence: Kamauli charter records royal appointment and land in Kamarupa-mandala within Pragjyotisa-bhukti.
interpretation: Strong administrative hierarchy; no dated declaration of recovery of all older Kamarupa.
limitation: Keep c.1138,1139,1142 chronologies visible rather than asserting one unqualified year.

title: Sena claim of expelling a Kamarupa king
evidence: Deopara verse 20 says Vijayasena expelled the Kamarupa king.
interpretation: Another external pressure event; no province-wide annexation or exact border follows.
limitation: Opponent, battle site and precise campaign date are not supplied.

date_label: Later textual tradition; not an early conquest date
title: Ratnapitha in a Karatoya–Sankosh scheme
evidence: One later scheme places Ratnapitha between those rivers; other schemes differ.
interpretation: Cultural / sacred regional overlay, not a securely attested Varman or Pala administrative province.
map_representation: optional source-labelled overlay outside ownership timeline
limitation: No evidenced event shows Kamarupa acquiring, losing and reacquiring this whole precisely bounded unit.
